title: Regulator-facing evidence matrix for control plane and VPC
body:
Purpose:
This working doc is a seller-facing reference and a regulator/audit prep checklist that maps specific control plane claims to concrete evidence artifacts we can present for on-prem / VPC Private deployments. The goal: give field sellers and CSMs a short, repeatable script plus attachments to hand to legal/compliance reviewers and auditors so we reduce back-and-forth and accelerate procurement for regulated workloads.

Audience and usage notes:
- Primary: sales engineers, enterprise AEs, CSMs prepping renewal pitches, and partner solution architects.
- Secondary: legal and security reviewers who need an initial evidence packet before formal audits.
- Style: pragmatic, citation-oriented, with sample replies and attachments to reduce ambiguity. Treat as living: point to Confluence artifacts for finalized evidence.

How to use this doc (quick play):
1) Identify buyer risk bucket (data sovereignty, PII/PHI handling, auditability, encryption keys, isolation).
2) Pull the evidence row(s) below and attach 2–3 supporting artifacts (architecture diagram, audit log sample, KMS integration notes).
3) Use the "Regulator Q&A" script to triage questions and record open items to the PD Jira board (linked).
4) When buyer asks for legal-ops docs, hand off to Legal with the Evidence Summary PDF we generate from Confluence.

Evidence matrix (claim -> what we show -> artifact examples -> seller script)
1) Claim: Dedicated control plane runs in customer VPC (no traffic to hosted control plane).
   What we show: network flow diagram + ingress/egress guardrail list + deployment manifest sample
   Artifact examples: VPC architecture diagram (PNG), terraform snippet for control-plane endpoints, egress ACL sample
   Seller script: "For private mode we deploy a lightweight control-plane connector inside your VPC. Control traffic is over your subnets only — we provide the IaC snippet and an ingress/egress checklist for your network team to validate. If you want, our infra engineer can run the IaC in a staging VPC during POC."

2) Claim: Customer keys never leave customer KMS/HSM; Redwood never has access to plaintext or keys.
   What we show: KMS integration flow, flow of envelope encryption, proof-of-concept HSM attestation steps
   Artifact examples: sample KMS policy, HSM attestation checklist, architecture diagram labeled 'keys never exportable'
   Seller script: "We integrate with your KMS/HSM using envelope encryption — Redwood stores ciphertext only. We can share a short sequence diagram and a template KMS policy your security team can review. If you require a vault attestation, we can coordinate an HSM vendor joint technical call."

3) Claim: Audit logs and telemetry are customer-controlled and auditable.
   What we show: log schema, retention options, sample signed log export, SIEM integration examples (Splunk/ELK/Datadog)
   Artifact examples: syslog export demo file, example Elasticsearch ingestion pipeline, JWT-signed log fragment showing user-id and request-id
   Seller script: "All control-plane and request-level logs can be pushed to your SIEM. We provide schema and adapters; here's a sample export showing the fields your compliance team requested. For PII-sensitive workloads we can sanitize or redact at the point of export per your policy."

4) Claim: Model artifacts and private data do not leave the customer's environment unless explicitly enabled.
   What we show: data flow for model weights, inference-only endpoints, optional model pull policies, tenant isolation diagram
   Artifact examples: example runtime config with 'local-only' model flag, isolation test report, model custody checklist
   Seller script: "By default, model execution remains in customer-managed infrastructure. You can opt in to pull public model updates, otherwise we will not push new weights without a signed change order. We have a model custody checklist you can include in your SOPs."

5) Claim: Strong access controls and RBAC for operator tooling; separation of duties between Redwood and customer admins.
   What we show: RBAC matrix, SSO/SAML/OIDC integration samples, operator access workflow, conditional MFA policy recommendations
   Artifact examples: sample SAML metadata, RBAC CSV export, operator audit trail example
   Seller script: "Control plane operations are gated by RBAC. We support SAML/OIDC and can map roles to your existing identity provider. If you need, we can provide a CSV demonstrating default role mappings and an operator audit sample from a staging run."

6) Claim: Compliance-friendly configurations and controls to satisfy baseline frameworks (SOC2-ish, FedRAMP-light, HIPAA concerns).
   What we show: configuration matrix mapping to control families, example config snapshots that meet baseline controls, gap list and mitigation plan
   Artifact examples: configuration export (YAML), mapping spreadsheet to control families, whitepaper excerpt on how the control plane meets control objectives
   Seller script: "For initial procurement we provide a mapping of our controls to your SOC2/HIPAA controls and a short plan for closing any gaps. Many customers treat our private control plane as a covered system inside their existing attestation boundary."

Regulator Q&A: short, directly usable replies for common objections
Q: "How can we be sure no telemetry crosses your hosted systems?"
A: "In Private mode the control-plane connector only transmits encrypted heartbeats and orchestration tokens to your monitoring endpoints; no request or model content is routed through Redwood hosted services. We can provide packet captures from a staging deployment and an independent network engineer readout."

Q: "We require yearly penetration testing and access reviews. Will you support that?"
A: "Yes. We provide an annual security package and can either run a joint pentest with your third party or provide a targeted scope for your vendor. We also support operator access review exports for your auditors."

Q: "What if we need to demonstrate proof of deletion for customer data?"
A: "We maintain deletion logs and a verifiable deletion workflow. For Private deployments we can run a deletion proof — a signed manifest that lists object IDs, deletion timestamps, and operator IDs. We can hand that to your audit team under NDA."

Competitive notes & positioning levers (short)
- Differentiator: Explicit evidence-first pack for audits — sellers should emphasize 'we bring artifacts, not just promises'.
- Differentiator: Fine-grained control plane configurability (config-as-code) vs. competitors who only offer opaque managed VPC connectors.
- Negotiation levers: Offer extended log retention add-on, in-person onboarding session with an infra eng for $X, or joint pentest as a professional services SKU.
- Risk item vs. self-hosted open-source runtimes: customers often worry about upgrade cadence and security patches. Counter: provide patching cadence, CVE response SLA, and a single-threaded contact for emergency patches during pilot.

Open items / engineering asks (for PD/Jira)
- Provide a short, exportable "Evidence PDF" generator in Confluence that compiles the referenced artifacts into a single packet (Jira PD-4121).
- Add a packet-capture sanitized sample to the artifacts library for network teams.
- Produce a template KMS policy per major cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) and an HSM vendor note.

Sample attachment checklist for an initial legal pre-review (pack to hand to buyer):
- One-page evidence summary (this doc, converted)
- VPC architecture diagram for control plane
- KMS integration flow + sample policy
- Audit log sample + SIEM ingestion note
- RBAC CSV and SAML metadata sample
- Model custody & deletion workflow excerpt

Notes to self / seller quick tips:
- Bring two artifacts into first meeting: VPC architecture diagram and a sanitized audit log. Those answer ~60% of early compliance questions.
- Avoid technical minutiae in early legal conversations; focus on where evidence lives and who the point of contact is.
- If a buyer requests a change that touches our hosted telemetry design, tag product and infra immediately — those are higher-impact asks.

Appendix: example short email for legal ops intro (copy/paste)
Subject: Evidence packet for Redwood Private control plane (initial attachments)
Hi [Legal/Ops Lead],
Per our conversation, attached is an initial evidence packet for the proposed Private control plane deployment. It includes architecture diagrams, KMS integration notes, sample audit logs, and a short mapping to typical control families. If you want an on-call walkthrough (30–45m) with our infra engineer and a Redwood security reviewer, let me know a couple times that work and I’ll schedule.
Thanks,
[AE name] / Redwood Inference

End of doc.
